title: aristoteles.yaml
description: The one file of a dir: the people, the roles, the deciders and the limits of each model (the mechanism), and the settings of the UI with the commands of each model. The name of the dir is the name of its folder.

people.description: The people who decide. The UI and the CLI act as the person whose name is the git user.name of the dir.

models.description: The models that the roles name, by name: the commands of each (settings) and its limits (mechanism). A persistent role of any model runs in a terminal of its own; a disposable role runs as a subagent inside the terminal above it. Choose a stronger model for a role whose work needs more care.

roles.description: The roles of the dir. Each agent role names its model and its acts; one persistent role splits (it hosts each project).

decide.description: Who decides the results of a maker, when more than one role approves it.

retryMinutes.description: The minutes between the tries of the UI after a system problem. The default is 5.

hostWaitMinutes.description: The minutes that the UI waits for the words of the host about an item, before it shows the item raw. The default is 10.

outsideSourceHours.description: The hours that a revision of an outside source holds; after them, work next asks the agent to read the source again. The default is 72.

sound.description: Play a sound when a badge shows. The default is false.

theme.description: The theme of the UI. The default is light.

briefChars.description: The longest brief that the CLI prints, sized to the context window of the model. The brief counts the guide text of the role, so the limit needs room above it (about 6000 for a role that assigns nothing, 16000 for a role that splits).

rules.description: How many rules one review checks.

size.description: The lines of one result: all the lines of its file, or of its section, because one review checks all of it. A commit has no size limit.

act.description: One of do, review, approve, change, assign, or a word of authority: split (split, remake and close tasks, evaluate a stop, shorten a brief, host a project), direct (draft and revise directions), fit (fit roles: their words, their fitness, an adjustment).

assign.description: The roles that this role gives work to.

kind.description: A program runs a command on each report.

model.description: The name of an entry of the models table.

output.description: The form of a result, for example "<file>#<section>" or "<repo>@<commit>".

persistence.description: How an agent role runs, apart from its model: a persistent role gets a terminal of its own for the whole project; a disposable role runs as a subagent of a terminal. why: the reason, which the card of the role shows. A program has none.

icon.description: The icon of the role on its card.

deciders.description: A role, or one of { or: [...] }, { and: [...] }, { order: [...] }.

launch.description: The command that starts an agent; {session} is the session id that the UI gives it, {model} (optional) is the name of the model, and {prompt} (optional) is its first input, given as an argument.

resume.description: The command that continues a closed session; {session} is its id, {model} (optional) is the name of the model, and {prompt} (optional) is the retry input.

start.description: The first input of a persistent agent; it starts the skill. {agent} is the id of the agent (p1). The default: Use the work skill. You are {agent}: run work wait --by={agent}, and do what it prints.

skills.description: The skills folder of the AI tool, relative to the dir; work start links the work and assess skills there.

errors.description: Words in the output that show a failed session.

prompts.description: Words in the last output that show a prompt: the session waits for an answer.

silentMinutes.description: Minutes with no output and no work command that count as a failed session. The default is 10.

retryInput.description: The input that a restarted session gets as its argument; {agent} is the id of its agent. The default: System message, not from the person. Run work wait --by={agent}, and do what it prints.

limits.description: The limits of the model, under the part that checks them.
